newsitem.title: GERMANY: German winter crops prosper as rain spreads.
newsitem.headline: German winter crops prosper as rain spreads.

text.p: Lasting rainfall is helping German winter crops overcome the damaging effects of drought in March and April, the DWD meteorological office said on Friday.
Its weekly crop weather report said winter rapeseed was blooming and winter grains were developing well.
Current temperatures of around 10 to 15 degrees C were unusually cold for May but should rise to maximum levels of 20 to 25 degrees over the next seven days.
Maize plantings had been completed and newly sown beet and spring grain crops were developing according to schedule.
"The rain is excellent news," a DWD source said.
"The crops cannot go wrong now unless there is an unexpected heat wave in the summer."
He also noted that the unusually cold temperatures this year had helped to keep fungi and pests to a minimum.
